newsitem.title: USA: Ahmanson bests Washington Mutual bid for Great Western.
newsitem.headline: Ahmanson bests Washington Mutual bid for Great Western.

text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co. Monday raised the stakes in the takeover battle for Great Western Financial Corp., topping Washington Mutual Savings Bank's $6.6 billion proposal by $400 million.
Ahmanson, the nation's biggest thrift, had previously offered $6.1 billion for Great Western, but Washington Mutual made its higher bid -- which Great Western accepted -- on March 6.

Ahmanson said that based on the closing price of the shares of Washington Mutual and Ahmanson on Friday, its improved offer provides a premium of about $3 a share over the implied value of the Washington Mutual proposal.
Washington Mutual's stock fell 25 cents to $50.125 on Nasdaq at midday. Ahmanson was unchanged at $40.25 and Great Western edged up 37.5 cents to $45.875.
Ahmanson, based in Irwindale, Calif., said its latest offer establishes a floating exchange ratio for Great Western common shares linked to the market price for Ahmanson common shares.
Great Western stockholders would now receive, tax free, not less than 1.10 and not more than 1.20 common shares of Ahmanson for each common share of Great Western.
Ahmanson's previous offer, announced on Feb. 18, provided an exchange ratio of 1.05 Ahmanson common shares for each Great Western common share.
Based on the closing price of its stock on March 14, Ahmanson said, its latest exchange ratio is 1.20, worth $48.30 for each Great Western common share.
Ahmanson Chairman and Chief Executive Charles Rinehart said he was confident that "we can responsibly assume an additional $100 million in merger benefits through our combination" with Great Western.
"We believe that this is a proposal that Washington Mutual cannot match without increasing its own shareholders' dilution to what must be an unacceptable level," he said.
Ahmanson also said cost savings from the merger would be up by at least $50 million to $454 million.
Rinehart urged Great Western to provide Ahmanson nonpublic information which it had given to Washington Mutual, and to hold talks on a definitive merger immediately.
Ahmanson, with assets of nearly $50 billion, is the parent company of Home Savings of America, one of the nation's largest full-service consumer banks.
